chunks: And from him, from Fadala, from Aban, from Isma'il ibn al-Fadl, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about what I should say in my Witr prayer, so he said: "Whatever God has decreed upon your tongue and determined."

key_terms.وَتْرِي: Witr prayer (the odd-numbered prayer offered at night)

ai.seo_question: What should be recited in the Witr prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) offers a pragmatic legal ruling for the Witr prayer, emphasizing that the recitation should be whatever naturally flows from the tongue, as it is divinely decreed. This perspective alleviates the burden of rigid memorization, highlighting the Shia scholarly emphasis on ease (*yusr*) and the spiritual authenticity of spontaneous devotion over formulaic recitation. It reflects the broader principle that the heart's connection to God is validated by the natural expression of faith, provided it aligns with the prescribed structure of the prayer.
